:::{#thm-wlln}
#### Weak law of large numbers

Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be [IID](independence.qmd#def-iid) random variables
with population mean $\mean$ and finite variance $\ss > 0$,
and let $\samplemean{X}{n} \eqdef \avgin X_i$ be the sample mean.
Then the sample mean [converges in probability](#def-convergence-in-probability) to $\mean$
[@wikipedia_law_of_large_numbers]:

$$
\samplemean{X}{n} \inprob \mean
$$

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

@CaseBerg01 [Thm. 5.5.2].
:::

:::

::: proof

By @cor-mean-iid-moments, $\E{\samplemean{X}{n}} = \mean$ and $\Var{\samplemean{X}{n}} = \ss/n$.

Let the tolerance be $\varepsilon > 0$ and let the multiplier be $k \eqdef \varepsilon \sqrt{n} / \sdpar$,
so that $k \sdpar / \sqrt{n} = \varepsilon$.
[Chebyshev's inequality](#thm-chebyshev) for $\samplemean{X}{n}$,
whose standard deviation is $\sdpar / \sqrt{n}$, gives

$$
\ba
0 \le \Prf{\abs{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean} \ge \varepsilon}
&= \Prf{\abs{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean} \ge k \frac{\sdpar}{\sqrt{n}}}
&& \text{(definition of $k$)}\\
&\le \frac{1}{k^2}
&& \text{(Chebyshev's inequality)}\\
&= \frac{\ss}{n \varepsilon^2}
&& \text{(substitute $k$)}
\ea
$$

The bound goes to zero as $n \to \infty$,
so the probability, squeezed between zero and the bound, goes to zero.
This holds for every $\varepsilon > 0$.

:::
